symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of vertices in the fixed experimental network.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: A generic label, with \(a=1\) denoting the focal exposure and \(a=0\) denoting the comparison exposure.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The fixed adjacency matrix on the \(n\) experimental units.

symbols.name: \nu
symbols.def: The randomization distribution chosen before outcomes are observed.

symbols.name: f_i
symbols.def: The exposure mapping induced by \(G\) for unit \(i\).

symbols.name: Y_i(w)
symbols.def: The potential outcome of unit \(i\) under assignment \(w\).

symbols.name: \Pi
symbols.def: The diagonal matrix whose diagonal is \((\pi_{1,1},\ldots,\pi_{n,1},\pi_{1,0},\ldots,\pi_{n,0})\).

symbols.name: Y_i(a)
symbols.def: The potential outcome of unit \(i\) under exposure label \(a\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The superpopulation law of the pair \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) used only for ex ante basis choice.

symbols.name: F_a^{-1}
symbols.def: The generalized inverse of the marginal distribution function.

symbols.name: b_1
symbols.def: The coefficients multiplying the focal-exposure indicators.

symbols.name: b_0
symbols.def: The coefficients multiplying the comparison-exposure indicators.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: A fixed lower bound on the normalized smallest eigenvalue of \(S_B\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B_Z
symbols.def: The scale-quotiented block-separable bases for which \(S_B\) is positive definite.

symbols.name: g_B(c)
symbols.def: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the Zhao gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right]\).

symbols.name: \ell_B(c)
symbols.def: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the residual \(\ell_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]-g_B(c)\).

symbols.name: m_a
symbols.def: The number of independent unpaired pilot outcomes observed under exposure label \(a\).

symbols.name: Y^{P}_{j,a}
symbols.def: The \(j\)-th independent pilot draw from \(F_a\), with no cross-arm pairing.

symbols.name: \widehat r(B)
symbols.def: The criterion obtained from \(r(B)\) by replacing \(F_a,\mu_a,\sigma_a^2,c_L,c_U\) with their empirical-marginal analogues from \(\widehat F_a\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}
symbols.def: An exact rational or real-algebraic encoding, or a certified inclusion-oracle encoding with effective refinement moduli and exact feasibility decisions, of \(\Pi,\Omega,c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\), with \(\varepsilon\) represented exactly.

symbols.name: B_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: An exactly feasible basis returned by the certified global solver at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: L_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A rational lower bound on \(v^\star\) certified by the feasible incumbent.

symbols.name: U_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A rational upper bound on \(v^\star\) obtained from outward-rounded bounds on every retained quotient-chart box.

symbols.name: h_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: The maximum projective-chart diameter of a box retained at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_\varepsilon
symbols.def: The union of unpruned quotient-chart boxes returned at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: \mathscr K_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: The returned record containing a finite quotient-chart cover, \(B_{\varepsilon}\), \(L_{\varepsilon}\), \(U_{\varepsilon}\), outward-rounded bounds, discarded-box records, retained boxes forming \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), and mesh \(h_{\varepsilon}\).

symbols.name: \xi
symbols.def: The instance \(\xi=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) with \(G\) and the exposure maps held fixed.

symbols.name: \mathfrak X_\kappa
symbols.def: The relatively topologized class of instances satisfying the named predicates ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility.

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: A positive certified lower bound on the robust-versus-surrogate separation.

symbols.name: \eta
symbols.def: A uniform positive lower bound on the excess of normalized basis nondegeneracy over \(\kappa\) across both optimizer correspondences.

assumptions.condition: For every unit \(i\) and assignments \(w,w'\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(f_i(w)=f_i(w')\) implies \(Y_i(w)=Y_i(w')\).
For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
The \(n\) pairs \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) have joint law \(H^{\otimes n}\).

standard.name: Independent and identically distributed potential-outcome pairs, Zhao Assumption 3\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 22

assumptions.condition: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
The ordered pair of marginals of \(H\) equals \((F_1,F_0)\).
The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).

standard.name: Sharp Fréchet covariance range, Aronow--Green--Lee Lemma 1

assumptions.condition: The pair \(\left(F_1\otimes F_0,\operatorname{Cov}_{F_1\otimes F_0}\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)\) belongs to \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\times\{0\}\).

standard.name: Independent product coupling with zero covariance
Supplied-basis control-variate nondegeneracy, Zhao Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21

assumptions.condition: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).

novel.justification: Independent rescaling of either basis column leaves Zhao's control-variate span and gain unchanged, so this condition selects compact representatives without restricting implementable estimators.

standard.name: Supplied-basis nondegeneracy, fixed-threshold variant of Zhao Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21

assumptions.condition: There exist vectors \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\) and \(\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B\}\ge\kappa\) for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).

novel.justification: This is a verifiable design-side condition: for a fixed network, exposure maps, and known randomization, the matrix \(\Omega\) is known before outcomes are observed, so nonemptiness of the normalized \(\kappa\)-regular projective class can be certified as part of design preparation. Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) regulates a supplied basis and does not assert existence of such a normalized feasible basis.

assumptions.condition: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).

novel.justification: Separate exposure-specific historical samples are available in insurance and public-health deployments even when privacy or record linkage prevents cross-arm pairing; independence from the later randomized assignment is ensured by collecting or freezing those archives before randomization. Mikhaeil and Green inform consistency of empirical marginal endpoints, not this product sampling law.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_Z
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_\kappa
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.

definitions.name: g_B(c),\ell_B(c)
definitions.construction: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\) and \(\ell_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]-g_B(c)\), both in \([0,\infty)\).

definitions.name: \mathcal A_R,\mathcal A_0
definitions.construction: On the feasible covariance domain, where ass:product-coupling-zero and ass:frechet-covariance-domain give \(0\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\), set \(\mathcal A_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) and the ordinarily typed surrogate correspondence \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}
definitions.construction: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary; require the tolerance \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.

definitions.name: \mathscr K_{\varepsilon}
definitions.construction: Return \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) as a finite quotient-chart cover together with an exactly feasible incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\); rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}\); outward-rounded objective and constraint bounds for every retained box; a checkable exact-infeasibility or valid upper-bound pruning record for every discarded box; retained boxes whose union is \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\); and their maximum chart diameter \(h_{\varepsilon}\). The checker requires \(L_{\varepsilon}\le r(B_{\varepsilon})\le v^\star\le U_{\varepsilon}\), \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), and never discards a box meeting the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary without an exact infeasibility or pruning certificate.

definitions.name: projective interval branch-and-bound handle
definitions.construction: Given \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), cover each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisect a retained box of maximum chart diameter, handle the sphere equations and \(\kappa\)-boundary with the exact feasibility interface, and bound both endpoint gains and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions and interval-Hessian underestimators. Maintain an exactly feasible incumbent, prune only with a checkable record, and continue maximum-diameter refinement until both \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), returning \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\).

definitions.name: \widehat r,\widehat v,\widehat{\mathcal A}_R
definitions.construction: Compute the empirical means, variances, and the two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\); substitute them into \(Q(c)\), \(g_B(c)\), and \(r(B)\); then set \(\widehat v=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak X_\kappa
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak X_\kappa=\{\xi=(\nu,F_1,F_0):\operatorname{ass{:}exposure\mbox{-}positivity}(\xi)\wedge\operatorname{ass{:}kappa\mbox{-}feasibility}(\xi)\wedge F_1,F_0\in\mathcal P([0,1])\}\) is carved by the single named positivity and feasibility predicates, with the relative topology inherited from total variation on the finite assignment simplex and the Wasserstein metric on each bounded marginal.

definitions.name: finite lawful separation handle
definitions.construction: Start from a three-vertex network under independent Bernoulli assignment with probability \(1/3\), enumerate the mutually exclusive exposure truth tables exactly, derive exact \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), use Bernoulli \(1/2\) pilot marginals, and run the certified projective interval handle simultaneously over the full robust and zero-covariance argmax correspondences. Search for rational certificates \(\delta>0\) and \(\eta>0\) that bound the correspondence-level loss separation and the optimizer-wide strict \(\kappa\)-slack.

statements.statement: Under ass:known-exposure, ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, and ass:iid-potential-pairs, every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) has affine functions \(c\mapsto g_B(c)\) and \(c\mapsto\ell_B(c)\) on the imported feasible domain \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\). Consequently, \(\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}\ell_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\), with both extrema attained. The product coupling gives \(c_L\le0\le c_U\), so \(g_B(0)\) is an ordinarily typed feasible-covariance gain. If \(c_L<0<c_U\), \(g_B(0)=\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})\) if and only if the affine slope of \(g_B\) is zero.
statements.justification: The theorem imports the published Fréchet range and proves its exact affine reduction inside Zhao's basis objective.
statements.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1, already gives the sharp covariance range. Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Theorem 4 and equation (8) on pp. 22--23, gives the covariance-dependent basis objective, and the paragraph following Theorem 4 on p. 23 substitutes the feasible zero-covariance surrogate matrix; neither source derives the affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside this projective objective.
statements.consumer: An experimenter with only two pilot marginals can evaluate the exact worst-copula gain of any proposed network basis.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By ass:exposure-positivity, \(\Pi\) is invertible.  If \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), then the defining nondegeneracy condition for \(\mathcal B_Z\) gives \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\), so \(S_B^{-1}\) exists.  Put
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\ I_n&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1},\qquad
A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
The moment-matrix construction gives the exact identity
\[
Q(c)=Q(0)-cE.
\]
Cyclicity of trace and def:gain-loss therefore yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
g_B(c)
&=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{A_BQ(c)\}\\
&=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{A_BQ(0)\}
-c\,n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_BE),
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\ell_B(c)
&=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{(A_{\mathrm{HT}}-A_B)Q(c)\}\\
&=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{(A_{\mathrm{HT}}-A_B)Q(0)\}
-c\,n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{(A_{\mathrm{HT}}-A_B)E\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus both maps are affine in \(c\).  The assumptions ass:known-exposure, ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, and ass:iid-potential-pairs supply the causal and ex ante interpretation of the moment and loss constructions; the displayed affine reduction is algebraic, with every inverse justified above.

By ass:frechet-covariance-domain and the definition of the covariance image,
\[
\bigl\{\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}:H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\bigr\}
=[c_L,c_U].
\]
An affine real-valued function on this closed interval attains its minimum and maximum at endpoints.  Equality of the covariance image with the closed interval also implies that each endpoint is the covariance of at least one coupling in \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\).  Applying these facts to the two displayed affine functions proves
\[
\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B\!\left(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)
=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}
\]
and
\[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}\ell_B\!\left(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)
=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\},
\]
with both extrema attained by endpoint couplings.

By ass:product-coupling-zero, the product coupling belongs to \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\) and has covariance zero.  Combining this with ass:frechet-covariance-domain gives \(0\in[c_L,c_U]\), equivalently \(c_L\le0\le c_U\), and hence \(g_B(0)\) is evaluated at a feasible covariance.

Finally, write \(g_B(c)=\alpha_B+\beta_Bc\), where
\[
\beta_B=-n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_BE).
\]
If \(\beta_B=0\), then \(g_B\) is constant, so its value at zero equals its infimum.  Conversely, suppose \(c_L<0<c_U\).  If \(\beta_B>0\), then
\[
g_B(c_L)=g_B(0)+\beta_Bc_L<g_B(0),
\]
whereas if \(\beta_B<0\), then
\[
g_B(c_U)=g_B(0)+\beta_Bc_U<g_B(0).
\]
Thus equality of \(g_B(0)\) with the worst-coupling gain is impossible unless \(\beta_B=0\).  This proves the stated equivalence. \(\square\)

statements.statement: For every \(\kappa>0\), the quotient \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is compact and satisfies \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\). Conversely, every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) has normalized representatives belonging to \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) for some basis-dependent \(\kappa>0\), so \(\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa=\mathcal B_Z\).
statements.justification: The proposition states exactly what the computational regularity restriction loses and recovers.
statements.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21, imposes boundedness and \(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\lambda_\Omega n\) on a supplied basis, but does not establish existence of a normalized feasible basis or construct a compact projective exhaustion for global optimization.
statements.consumer: Certified solvers can report the regularity threshold alongside the basis instead of presenting an undocumented numerical trim.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(\kappa>0\), and let
\[
K_\kappa=\left\{(b_1,b_0)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n:
\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n,\ 
\lambda_{\min}\!\left(n^{-1}B(b_1,b_0)^{\top}\Omega B(b_1,b_0)\right)\ge\kappa
\right\}.
\]
The product of the two radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres is compact.  The map
\[
(b_1,b_0)\longmapsto B(b_1,b_0)^{\top}\Omega B(b_1,b_0)
\]
is continuous, and the smallest-eigenvalue map is continuous on symmetric matrices.  Hence \(K_\kappa\) is a closed subset of that compact product and is compact, including when it is empty.  Let \(q\) be the quotient map that identifies independent nonzero rescalings of the two columns.  By def:kappa-basis-class, \(\mathcal B_\kappa=q(K_\kappa)\).  Since \(q\) is continuous for the quotient topology, \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is compact.

For every \((b_1,b_0)\in K_\kappa\),
\[
\lambda_{\min}\{B(b_1,b_0)^{\top}\Omega B(b_1,b_0)\}
\ge n\kappa>0.
\]
Thus its block-separable basis satisfies the nondegeneracy predicate in def:zhao-basis-class, proving \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).

Conversely, take a projective class \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\), represented as
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}.
\]
The condition \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\) implies \(b_1\ne0\) and \(b_0\ne0\).  Define
\[
d_a=\frac{\sqrt n}{\lVert b_a\rVert_2}\quad(a\in\{1,0\}),
\qquad T=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_0),
\qquad \widetilde B=BT.
\]
Then \(\widetilde B\) represents the same projective class as \(B\), and its two columns satisfy ass:projective-normalization.  Furthermore,
\[
S_{\widetilde B}=\widetilde B^{\top}\Omega\widetilde B
=T S_B T\succ0,
\]
because congruence by the invertible matrix \(T\) preserves positive definiteness.  Consequently
\[
\rho_B=\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_{\widetilde B})>0.
\]
Taking \(\kappa_B=\rho_B/2>0\), the normalized representative \(\widetilde B\) satisfies
\[
\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_{\widetilde B})\ge\kappa_B,
\]
so \([B]\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_B}\).  Thus every element of \(\mathcal B_Z\) belongs to \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) for some basis-dependent \(\kappa>0\).  Together with the first inclusion, this proves
\[
\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa=\mathcal B_Z.
\]
\(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) satisfies \(\Delta(\xi_0)>0\) and there is \(\eta>0\) such that \(\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_R(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\}\ge\eta\), then there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) of \(\xi_0\) such that \(\Delta(\xi)>0\) for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\).
statements.justification: Persistence upgrades any exact finite witness from a curiosity to a nondegenerate region of lawful experiments.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals gives continuity of fixed-marginal coupling correspondences, while GaoKleywegt2017DependenceRobust gives a general dependence-robust decision template; neither proves strict robust-basis dominance for Zhao's optimizer correspondences.
statements.consumer: Any certified output of oeq:separated-lawful-witness with \(\delta>0\) and optimizer-wide slack \(\eta>0\) activates this theorem and yields a relative-open region on which every robust optimizer has lower worst-copula residual variance than every zero-covariance-surrogate optimizer.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Write \(K(\xi)=\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi)\) for the normalized feasible projective class at instance \(\xi\).  We first record the relevant joint continuities.  On the finite assignment space, total-variation convergence of \(\nu_j\) to \(\nu\) implies entrywise convergence of \(\Pi_j\) and \(\Omega_j\).  At every exposure-positive \(\xi\), all diagonal entries of \(\Pi\) are strictly positive; therefore \(\Pi_j^{-1}\to\Pi^{-1}\) for \(j\) sufficiently large.  If \(F_{a,j}\to F_a\) in the Wasserstein metric on \([0,1]\), their quantiles satisfy
\[
\int_0^1\left|F_{a,j}^{-1}(u)-F_a^{-1}(u)\right|\,du\longrightarrow0.
\tag{1}
\]
Because all quantiles lie in \([0,1]\),
\[
\left|\int_0^1q_{1,j}(u)q_{0,j}(u)\,du-
\int_0^1q_1(u)q_0(u)\,du\right|
\le \lVert q_{1,j}-q_1\rVert_1+\lVert q_{0,j}-q_0\rVert_1,
\tag{2}
\]
and the same inequality holds with the second quantile evaluated at \(1-u\).  The marginal means and second moments also converge.  Hence \(c_L,c_U,Q(c_L),Q(c_U)\) vary continuously with \(\xi\).

For normalized representatives \((b_1,b_0)\) on the product of radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres, the map
\[
(\xi,B)\longmapsto \lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega(\xi)B\}
\tag{3}
\]
is continuous.  On its superlevel set at \(\kappa>0\), the inverse obeys
\[
\lVert S_B(\xi)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le(n\kappa)^{-1}.
\tag{4}
\]
The finite-dimensional formulas in def:gain-loss, together with (1)--(4), therefore show that
\[
(\xi,B)\longmapsto g_{B,\xi}(0),\quad
(\xi,B)\longmapsto r_\xi(B),\quad
(\xi,B)\longmapsto w_\xi(B)
\tag{5}
\]
are jointly continuous on the feasible graph.  The minimum and maximum over two endpoints preserve continuity.

We next prove upper stability of both optimizer correspondences directly.  Let \(\xi_j\to\xi_0\) in \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\), let \(B_j\in\mathcal A_R(\xi_j)\), and suppose along a subsequence that \(B_j\to B\) in the compact normalized projective quotient.  Feasibility and (3) give \(B\in K(\xi_0)\).  Choose any \(B^\circ\in\mathcal A_R(\xi_0)\).  The slack hypothesis gives
\[
\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}S_{B^\circ}(\xi_0)\}\ge\kappa+\eta.
\]
By (3), the fixed basis \(B^\circ\) belongs to \(K(\xi_j)\) for every sufficiently large \(j\).  Empirical optimality at \(\xi_j\) and (5) then give
\[
r_{\xi_j}(B_j)\ge r_{\xi_j}(B^\circ)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
r_{\xi_0}(B)\ge r_{\xi_0}(B^\circ)=\max_{C\in K(\xi_0)}r_{\xi_0}(C).
\]
Thus \(B\in\mathcal A_R(\xi_0)\).  Replacing \(r\) and \(B^\circ\) by \(g(0)\) and any member of \(\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)\) proves the analogous assertion for \(\mathcal A_0\).  The optimizer-wide slack assumed in the theorem supplies the fixed strictly feasible comparator in both cases.

The optimizer sets are nonempty and compact because every \(K(\xi)\) is nonempty and compact and both objectives are continuous.  For each \(j\), choose
\[
B_{0,j}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B),
\qquad
B_{R,j}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal A_R(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B).
\]
Every subsequence has a further subsequence on which both bases converge.  The preceding optimizer-stability argument and (5) show that any such limits \(B_0,B_R\) lie in \(\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)\) and \(\mathcal A_R(\xi_0)\), respectively.  Consequently,
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B)
\ge \inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B)
\tag{6}
\]
and
\[
\limsup_{j\to\infty}\sup_{B\in\mathcal A_R(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B)
\le \sup_{B\in\mathcal A_R(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B).
\tag{7}
\]
Subtracting (7) from (6) yields
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)\ge\Delta(\xi_0)>0.
\tag{8}
\]
The relative topology on \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\) is metrizable by the stated product metrics.  If no relative-open neighborhood with positive gap existed, one could choose \(\xi_j\to\xi_0\) with \(\Delta(\xi_j)\le0\), contradicting (8).  Hence the required relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) exists. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Can the construction in def:separation-search-handle produce explicit \(G\), exposure maps \(f_i\), assignment law \(\nu\), marginals \(F_1,F_0\), and threshold \(\kappa\), together with exact \(\Pi,\Omega,c_L,c_U\), checkable exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility certificates, and rational \(\delta,\eta>0\) such that the induced \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) satisfies \(\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_0)-\sup_{B_R\in\mathcal A_R(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_R)\ge\delta\) and \(\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_R(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\}\ge\eta\), with both bounds certified over the full argmax correspondences?
statements.justification: This correspondence-level certificate is the early kill test for whether strict dominance and the persistence hypothesis hold at any lawful finite design.
statements.gap: No located paper supplies a lawful network instance with a certified separation between full robust and nominal optimizer correspondences; a hand-picked pair of bases would not establish the required claim.
statements.consumer: Only a positive separation-and-slack certificate licenses the downstream open-neighborhood result and a strict-dominance interpretation in the Jiangxi application.

statements.statement: Fix \(G,\nu,(f_i)_{i=1}^n\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility, so \(\mathcal B_\kappa\neq\varnothing\). Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, as \(m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty\), \(\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}|\widehat r(B)-r(B)|\to0\) almost surely, \(\widehat v\to v^\star\) almost surely, and every subsequential limit of \(B_m\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) belongs to \(\mathcal A_R\) almost surely. Equivalently, \(\limsup_{m_1,m_0\to\infty}\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\subseteq\mathcal A_R\) almost surely in the projective quotient.
statements.justification: The set-valued conclusion is the strongest valid generic guarantee when projective symmetries or endpoint ties create multiple optimizers.
statements.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance and MikhaeilGreen2024SharpRegressionAdjustment prove scalar endpoint consistency; Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Theorem 3, concerns estimated-coefficient consistency and asymptotics but does not establish uniform global basis-objective or argmax-correspondence consistency.
statements.consumer: An independent historical or external pilot can select a robust network basis without pretending that its two marginal samples identify a cross-world copula.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix normalized representatives of the projective classes in \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  By prop:kappa-exhaustion and ass:kappa-feasibility this is a nonempty compact space.  For every such representative, the two columns of \(B\) have disjoint block supports and squared norm \(n\), while membership in \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) gives
\[
\lVert B\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=\sqrt n,
\qquad
\lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le (n\kappa)^{-1}.
\tag{1}
\]
Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  All design matrices in what follows are fixed.

We first establish convergence of every pilot ingredient.  Write \(q_a=F_a^{-1}\) and \(\widehat q_a=\widehat F_a^{-1}\).  For a bounded i.i.d. sequence and any bounded scalar transform, the strong law follows here from a fourth-moment argument.  If \(X_j\) are independent, centered, and \(|X_j|\le1\), then
\[
\mathbb E\left(\sum_{j=1}^mX_j\right)^4
=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E X_j^4
+6\sum_{j<k}\mathbb E X_j^2\,\mathbb E X_k^2
\le 3m^2.
\]
Markov's inequality gives
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\left|m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^mX_j\right|>t\right)
\le \frac{3}{m^2t^4}.
\]
The sum of these bounds over \(m\) is finite, and the union bound applied to all events with \(m\ge M\), followed by \(M\to\infty\), shows that only finitely many occur almost surely.  Apply this simultaneously, over the countable rational \(x\), to \(\mathbf 1\{Y^P_{j,a}\le x\}\).  Monotonicity then yields \(\widehat F_a(x)\to F_a(x)\) at every continuity point of \(F_a\).  The generalized-inverse squeeze yields \(\widehat q_a(u)\to q_a(u)\) at every continuity point of \(q_a\).  A monotone function has at most countably many discontinuities, and all quantiles lie in \([0,1]\); splitting the integral outside a set of arbitrarily small measure on which convergence is uniform therefore gives
\[
\int_0^1|\widehat q_a(u)-q_a(u)|\,du\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely},\qquad a\in\{1,0\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The same bounded strong law, applied to \(Y^P_{j,a}\) and \((Y^P_{j,a})^2\), gives \(\widehat\mu_a\to\mu_a\) and \(\widehat\sigma_a^2\to\sigma_a^2\) almost surely.  Since all quantiles are bounded by one,
\[
\left|\int_0^1\widehat q_1(u)\widehat q_0(u)\,du-
\int_0^1q_1(u)q_0(u)\,du\right|
\le\lVert\widehat q_1-q_1\rVert_1+\lVert\widehat q_0-q_0\rVert_1,
\tag{3}
\]
and the identical bound holds with the second quantile evaluated at \(1-u\).  Equations (2)--(3), together with convergence of the means, imply
\[
\widehat c_L\to c_L,
\qquad
\widehat c_U\to c_U
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{4}
\]
This uses only the two marginal samples and never estimates a cross-world copula.

For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), let \(Q_e=Q(c_e)\) and let \(\widehat Q_e\) be its plug-in version, including the plug-in means and variances.  The finite-dimensional formula in def:moment-matrix and (4) imply
\[
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q_e\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{5}
\]
Put \(C_\nu=\lVert\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\), which is finite because \(n\) is fixed and \(\Pi\) is invertible.  The inequality \(|\operatorname{tr}(A)|\le2\lVert A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\) for a \(2\times2\) matrix, def:gain-loss, and (1) yield, uniformly over \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\),
\[
|\widehat g_B(\widehat c_e)-g_B(c_e)|
\le \frac{2}{n^2}\lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\lVert B\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2 C_\nu^2
\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q_e\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le \frac{2C_\nu^2}{n^2\kappa}
\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q_e\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{6}
\]
The minimum map is one-Lipschitz in the sup norm.  Hence (5)--(6) give
\[
\delta_m:=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}
|\widehat r(B)-r(B)|\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely as }m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty.
\tag{7}
\]

Both endpoint gains are continuous on \(\mathcal B_\kappa\): matrix inversion is continuous on the uniformly positive-definite set in (1), and the remaining operations are finite-dimensional and continuous.  Thus \(r\) and \(\widehat r\) are continuous and attain their maxima on the compact quotient.  The elementary maximum inequality and (7) show
\[
|\widehat v-v^\star|
=\left|\max_B\widehat r(B)-\max_Br(B)\right|
\le\delta_m\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{8}
\]
Finally, take any sequence with \(m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty\), any \(B_m\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\), and a convergent subsequence \(B_{m_j}\to B_\infty\), which exists by compactness.  For any \(B^\star\in\mathcal A_R\), empirical optimality and (7) imply
\[
r(B_{m_j})\ge\widehat r(B_{m_j})-\delta_{m_j}
\ge\widehat r(B^\star)-\delta_{m_j}
\ge r(B^\star)-2\delta_{m_j}=v^\star-2\delta_{m_j}.
\]
Continuity gives \(r(B_\infty)=v^\star\), so \(B_\infty\in\mathcal A_R\).  This is exactly \(\limsup\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\subseteq\mathcal A_R\) in the compact projective quotient, and proves all assertions. \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal A_R=\{B^\star\}\) in the projective quotient, \(B^\star\) is isolated by a positive objective gap outside every neighborhood, and exactly one of \(c_L,c_U\) attains \(r(B^\star)\), then every measurable selection \(\widehat B\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) converges almost surely to \(B^\star\). Without the singleton condition, there exist bounded two-marginal instances satisfying the maintained assumptions for which the outer-set conclusion of thm:plugin-correspondence holds but some measurable plug-in selections fail to converge to a point.
statements.justification: This proposition draws the exact line between defensible set consistency and unjustified point consistency.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals implies upper hemicontinuity for optimizer sets but does not give this pilot-based quotient-space selection result or its tie counterexample.
statements.consumer: Applied reporting can retain all empirically indistinguishable robust bases unless an isolated unique saddle is actually verified.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Work on the probability-one event on which all conclusions of thm:plugin-correspondence hold.  Let \(U\) be any neighborhood of \(B^\star\) in the compact projective quotient.  The asserted isolation supplies
\[
\gamma_U:=v^\star-\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\setminus U}r(B)>0.
\tag{1}
\]
Let \(\delta_m=\sup_B|\widehat r(B)-r(B)|\), so \(\delta_m\to0\) by thm:plugin-correspondence.  If \(2\delta_m<\gamma_U\), then every \(B\notin U\) satisfies
\[
\widehat r(B)\le r(B)+\delta_m
\le v^\star-\gamma_U+\delta_m
< v^\star-\delta_m
\le\widehat r(B^\star).
\]
Consequently \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\subset U\) for all sufficiently large pilot sizes.  Since \(U\) was arbitrary, every measurable selection \(\widehat B\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) converges almost surely to \(B^\star\).  The hypothesis that exactly one endpoint is active labels the limiting saddle unambiguously; it is not needed for convergence of the basis once the singleton and gap hypotheses hold.

It remains to show that generic point convergence cannot replace the outer-set conclusion.  Consider the following bounded instance.  Let \(n=3\), take the empty network, put \(f_i(w)=w_i\), and draw the coordinates of \(W\) independently as Bernoulli \(1/2\).  Then \(D_{i,1}=W_i\), \(D_{i,0}=1-W_i\), exposure positivity holds, and
\[
\Pi=\frac12I_6,
\qquad
\Omega=\frac14
\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix}.
\tag{2}
\]
Let \(F_1=F_0=\delta_0\), let the potential-outcome pairs have law \(H=\delta_{(0,0)}\), and use the corresponding independent unpaired pilot samples.  These outcomes are bounded, all pilots equal zero, and
\[
\mu_1=\mu_0=\sigma_1^2=\sigma_0^2=c_L=c_U=0,
\qquad Q(0)=0.
\tag{3}
\]
Choose \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(e_1,e_2,e_3\) the coordinate vectors of \(\mathbb R^3\), define
\[
B^{(2)}=B(\sqrt3e_1,\sqrt3e_2),
\qquad
B^{(3)}=B(\sqrt3e_1,\sqrt3e_3).
\]
For either basis, (2) gives
\[
S_{B^{(j)}}=\frac34I_2,
\qquad
\lambda_{\min}\{3^{-1}S_{B^{(j)}}\}=\frac14>\kappa.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus ass:kappa-feasibility holds, and the two displayed bases are distinct points of the projective quotient.  By (3), however, \(g_B(0)=r(B)=0\) for every \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\).  The empirical moments and endpoints are identically zero for every pilot size, so also \(\widehat r(B)=0\) for every feasible \(B\).  Therefore
\[
\widehat{\mathcal A}_R=\mathcal A_R=\mathcal B_\kappa
\quad\text{for every pilot size}.
\tag{5}
\]
Along \(m_1=m_0=m\), choose the deterministic, hence measurable, selection \(\widehat B_m=B^{(2)}\) for even \(m\) and \(\widehat B_m=B^{(3)}\) for odd \(m\).  It has two distinct subsequential limits and hence no point limit, whereas (5) makes the outer-set conclusion hold exactly.  This supplies the required bounded two-marginal counterexample. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
The universal certified-solver conclusion is false for the interface \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) as defined.  In particular, let \(n=3\), let \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\) variables under \(\nu\), and set \(f_i(w)=w_i\).  With \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\varepsilon=1/10\), the two marginal pairs \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\) and \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_1,\delta_0)\) produce the same encoded tuple
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,\qquad
\Omega=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix},
\qquad c_L=c_U=0,
\]
but their robust values satisfy \(v^\star=0\) and \(v^\star\ge1/3\), respectively.  Consequently, no algorithm whose only input is \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) can always return rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon}\le v^\star\le U_{\varepsilon}\) with \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\); hence the conjunction requested in oeq:certified-global-basis does not hold.

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite network \(G\), known assignment law \(\nu\), known exposure maps \(f_i\), and two mutually exclusive exposure events.
sampling_model.units: The realized finite-population potential outcomes are fixed for design-based estimation; the i.i.d. law \(H\) is used only to choose the basis ex ante.
sampling_model.treatment: The main experiment draws \(W\sim\nu\), and assignment is the only randomness in the causal estimator conditional on the chosen basis.
sampling_model.overlap: Every exposure probability \(\pi_{i,a}\) is positive, and basis covariance is bounded below by \(\kappa\) on the optimization class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Two arm-specific external or historical i.i.d. samples are mutually unpaired and independent of the later assignment; they estimate \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), while the cross-world copula is neither estimated nor assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The network-interference optimal basis maximizes a nonconvex projective gain depending on the cross-potential-outcome covariance, while implementation sets that unidentified covariance to zero.
Comonotone and countermonotone quantile couplings attain sharp covariance and difference-in-means variance endpoints for two fixed marginals.
Empirical adjusted-outcome marginals consistently estimate sharp regression-adjusted variance endpoints.
Admissible conservative quadratic variance bounds under arbitrary interference can be selected through convex optimization for many objectives.
A branch-and-bound algorithm attains finite epsilon-global termination for bounded nonconvex all-quadratic programs.
Interval curvature bounds and convex underestimators yield deterministic global convergence for twice-differentiable constrained nonlinear programs.

tldr: Rare network exposures make Horvitz--Thompson estimation noisy, and Zhao's optimal indicator control variates reduce this design variance, but the ex ante basis depends on a cross-world covariance that an unpaired pilot cannot identify. The contribution chain imports the sharp Fréchet covariance range, proves a new fixed-basis affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's objective, poses certified global maximin optimization on the fixed-\(\kappa\) projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency without assuming away ties. Neighborhood persistence is supporting and witness-gated; no strict-dominance region is claimed unless the full-correspondence separation-and-slack certificate is produced.

project_justification.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates explicitly leaves robust basis choice under moment misspecification open; existing Fréchet results identify covariance endpoints, and existing global-optimization results certify Euclidean-box programs, but no paper joins these steps for a block-separable network basis with projective symmetry.
project_justification.niche: Two unpaired pilot marginals identify the exact dependence ambiguity relevant to Zhao's moment matrix while leaving the experimental network and assignment law fixed and known.
project_justification.fill: The project imports the sharp endpoint formulas, proves their affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, formulates a computably specified global maximin certificate on the compact \(\kappa\)-regular projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency. Conditional persistence is supporting: a strict-dominance region requires a separate certified witness with both separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack.

related_work: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates is the direct anchor. Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21 regulates a supplied basis, Assumption 3\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 22 supplies the i.i.d. potential-outcome-pair model, Theorem 4 and equation (8) on pp. 22--23 give the covariance-dependent basis optimization, and the paragraph following Theorem 4 on p. 23 gives the zero-covariance surrogate; Theorem 3 is limited to estimated-coefficient consistency and asymptotics. AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance is imported background: Lemma 1 proves the sharp covariance range and its quantile-coupling attainment, while Proposition 1 establishes endpoint estimation. The product coupling \(F_1\otimes F_0\) is feasible and has covariance zero, so Zhao's surrogate is an ordinarily typed member of the same covariance domain. MikhaeilGreen2024SharpRegressionAdjustment informs empirical marginal-endpoint consistency through Proposition 1, but neither supplies the independent unpaired product sampling law nor treats interference and an ex ante basis argmax. Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals informs continuity of fixed-marginal coupling correspondences. Reeves1975GlobalQuadratic and AdjimanDallwigFloudasNeumaier1998AlphaBB inform the incumbent, region-bound, subdivision, and convex-underestimator logic, but do not cover the projective quotient, exact regularity boundary, or endpoint kink. HarshawMiddletonSavje2026 optimizes conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference; its object is the variance bound rather than the control-variate basis. GaoKleywegt2017DependenceRobust informs the decision-theoretic treatment of dependence ambiguity but studies generic stochastic losses. AronowSamii2017 supplies the exposure-mapping design foundation. CaiDeJanvrySadoulet2015 is the application source for the Jiangxi insurance network that Zhao reanalyzes.
technical_internal_limitation: The presolve fractions \(521/1200\), \(2613/8432\), and \(4912/39525\) are not formal claims because the triangle exposure truth tables, the resulting entries of \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), the value of \(\kappa\), full equality-set bounds, and optimizer-wide strict \(\kappa\)-slack certificate are not supplied. The early kill test is oeq:separated-lawful-witness over exact assignment enumeration and both full optimizer correspondences. Unnumbered sanity check and regression test: if \(F_1\) and \(F_0\) are point masses, then the definitions give \(c_L=c_U=0\), hence \(r(B)=g_B(0)\) and \(\mathcal A_R=\mathcal A_0\). Zhao's Corollary 3 supports the stronger noiseless inverse-probability-weighted basis special case, while this correspondence equality is only a definitional code check and carries no theorem or novelty status.
honest_scope: The sharp Fréchet covariance range is imported from AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1. The new theorem targets are its affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, projective compactness, uniform plug-in value and outer-set consistency, and conditional neighborhood persistence. The finite epsilon-global solver and the separated lawful witness are first-class open constructions. Persistence is incremental and yields a strict-dominance region only after the witness supplies both a positive full-correspondence separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack; no such region is otherwise claimed. No SDP reduction, universal minimax interchange, universal strict improvement, asymptotic normality for the pilot-selected basis, or point convergence under ties is claimed.
